description: Runs a smooth random voltage at a set rate, with three outputs carrying three different distributions, drawn from a seedable random source

params.text: Sets the seed, 0 to 1 across the seed range; at 0 the seed comes from the clock of the computer instead and every reset gives a fresh run
While on, the values are drawn over -5V to 5V; while off, over 0-10V
Sets how fast new values are reached, as a power of two in hertz, from about 0.004Hz to 256Hz
Sets how many uniform draws each value is made from, 1 to 20; at 1, marked Uniform, every output carries a plain uniform distribution
Sets how many channels the outputs carry, 1 to 16, unless a polyphonic cable in the FM jack sets a larger count
Attenuates the voltage at the jack above it before it is added to the rate, 0 to 100 per cent

inputs.text: A trigger here reseeds the random source from the Seed knob and refills the whole run of values, so the same run is heard again
Shifts the rate, one octave per volt scaled by the knob below it; a cable with more than one channel here also sets how many channels the outputs carry

outputs.text: The smallest of the draws, interpolated smoothly, which crowds the values towards the bottom of the range as Sth is raised
A Weibull distribution with its density set by Sth, interpolated smoothly
The average of the draws, interpolated smoothly, which crowds the values towards the middle of the range as Sth is raised and approaches a normal distribution

notes: the smooth curve through the drawn values overshoots them, so the outputs pass outside 0-10V in unipolar mode and outside -5V to 5V in bipolar mode

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
